I wanted to thank you in advance for your time and efforts. Based on the staff report and the recommendation of the Planning Commission, we will comply with all requirements listed by them. Chiron's Farm is a family-run agricultural operation on a 99-acre AR2 property.

We've operated here responsibly and quietly for many years, focusing on breeding and training German Shepherd dogs for service work, therapy, and stable family companionship. Our commitment to this breed began as a family experience, not a business decision.

I was raised with German Shepherds. They were my constant companions and our children's constant companions. When our six-month-old daughter became sick with pneumococcal meningitis and as a result became deaf. As she grew, we felt she needed help to become more confident and aware in this hearing world. We purchased a puppy from a police officer that lived near us. Our daughter was profoundly deaf, and our German Shepherd became her ears in this world. That bond helped her communicate, connect, and gain confidence. Seeing that transformation shaped how we view these dogs as true partners that changed our lives.

That experience guides how we breed and raise our dogs today. We work with the highest quality West German show lines because they're consistently produced the health structure, temperament, and sound nerves needed for service and therapy work.

Our dogs are raised with daily human interaction, socialization, and thoughtful care from the start. We have lived on our farm for 26 years, And for many of those years, we started a breeding program to raise GS puppies to help other people like they helped our daughter.

At the same time, Roger and I both have had professional careers of our own. We have operated in Loudoun County for many years and have passed regular and unannounced inspections by Loudoun County Animal Services, the USDA, and the American Kennel Club.

We remain fully compliant with all applicable regulations, and we encourage our adoptive families to stay in contact with us creating long-term trust and accountability we're requesting approval to continue our breeding program on our farm and to train the dogs we breed and raise we're also requesting a special exception to modify the setback along the north side of the property no land disturbance is required now or in the future for this endeavor and the use remains

consistent with the rural and agricultural character of the area our responsibility to our dogs is lifelong. Retired breeding dogs are either placed with approved families or remain in our care for life and we accept dogs back if a family can no longer keep them and we re-home them. Due to that policy our numbers became higher than the actual number of dogs that are in the breeding and service dog training program. This commitment directly affected our on-site numbers. All dogs

are housed indoors in existing kennel buildings with multiple layers of secure dog safe fencing. Puppies and whoopie mothers are kept separately in the nursery. All areas are climate controlled, clean, and continuously supervised with daily enrichment, training, and supervised outdoor play.

Care is provided by staff from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. with continuous oversight by family members who live on the property. Dogs follow structured daily routines that include training, enrichment, and supervised outdoor time. Cleaning and care occur throughout the day and dogs are brought back indoors promptly after exercise. The property is a 99-acre AR2 parcel and the kennel occupies only a small defined area on the north side. The surrounding environment is quiet and agricultural.

the kennel is more than 1300 feet from the public road and about half a mile from the nearest single family home dogs are housed indoors in sound attenuated buildings outdoor time is supervised and limited and daily enrichment and training help keep dogs calm fulfilled and quiet there's a minimum 15 foot natural tree line along the north property line and we've added more than 30 evergreen trees along the north side kennel area combined with distance these measures effectively

mitigate visual and sound impacts all client interactions are by appointment only traffic is limited to approximately 10 to 15 work-related trips per week or fewer similar to neighboring properties there are no boarding drop-offs or doggy daycare services provided kennel areas are cleaned and disinfected multiple times daily. Waste is bagged and removed regularly with no on-site disposal. Cleaning is done through spot cleaning rather than washdowns, preventing runoffs.

Waste is picked up in our commercial trash containers by Waste Management Weekly. Surrounding uses include farms, livestock, animal husbandry, and equestrian properties. The kennel use aligns with these agricultural practices.

Conservation areas are preserved, the tree growth is expanded annually, and wildlife habitat is supported. No expansion of the kennel is proposed. This year we planted 60 trees and well over 150 over the past few years.

Shiraz Farm is a family operation built on long-term responsibility, both to our dogs and to the land we care for. We are careful stewards of this property, and our farm is designed to preserve the rural character of the land without disturbance or expansion.
